text.p: Polish Development Bank (PBR) will postpone its planned issue of up to 4.7-million shares, partly for foreign institutional investors, PBR's president said on Tuesday.
Mieczyslaw Groszek told a news conference that if these institutional investors buy up the whole issue, they will have up to 20 percent of PBR's shares.

"The decision about the issue was taken at the general shareholders' meeting in December... the management decided not to carry out the issue in the near term because of the market's climate," Groszek said.
He explained the delay was due to falls on the Warsaw bourse and large offers on the primary market.

Groszek added negotiations with investors would be resumed after the state treasury sells Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA, expected by June 12. PBR is a consortium bidding for at least 51-percent of shares in PBK.
